title: Kirsten Corazzini named UNH senior executive director of healthcare strategy - NH Business Review
content: Kirsten Corazzini, dean of the University of New Hampshire’s College of Health and Human Services, has been named Senior Executive Director of Healthcare Strategy at UNH, effective Jan. 2, 2027. In her new role, Corazzini will direct the University System of New Hampshire’s GO-NORTH Rural Health Transformation Workforce Hub, a five-year initiative with funding of up to $97 million to strengthen healthcare workforce education and expand access to training in rural communities. She will oversee investments in clinical simulation training, expand educational pathways into healthcare professions, and develop partnerships to address workforce shortages, particularly in rural and underserved communities throughout New Hampshire. Corazzini joined UNH in 2022 and has led significant growth in the College of Health and Human Services’ academic programs, research, and statewide partnerships. Among her accomplishments was establishing UNH’s School of Nursing, which now serves approximately 800 students and whose undergraduate program recently earned a place among the nation’s top 100 in U.S. News & World Report’s rankings. She also led the expansion of the college’s research infrastructure and strengthened partnerships with Dartmouth University and Dartmouth Health, and Mass General Brigham. Under her leadership, the college advanced from unranked to a top-10 position among Schools of Allied Health in New England for National Institutes of Health funding. title: UnitedHealth UNH Stock Dives 20% as Breakup Pressure and Medicare Audit Threats Hit the Healthcare Insurers - FXLeaders
content: UnitedHealth UNH stock plunged to $320s as proposed Medicare audit reforms, political calls to break up healthcare conglomerates and rising medical costs threaten insurers’ earnings and margins. Healthcare stocks extended their decline on Wednesday after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed tougher oversight of Medicare, Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and the health insurance marketplace. UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) has been among the hardest hit, falling approximately 20% in three sessions and slipping below $330. Proposed Medicare Advantage audit reforms, political pressure to break up large healthcare conglomerates and rising medical costs are combining to undermine investor confidence in the sector. A major catalyst emerged on November 16, when CMS proposed the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare, or CRUSH rule. The proposal would formalise risk-adjustment data validation audits and allow regulators to extrapolate findings from sampled claims across entire Medicare Advantage contracts. Audits could extend back to payment year 2018, with CMS estimating that the framework could recover approximately $9 billion annually across the industry. UnitedHealth faces considerable exposure because it operates the country’s largest Medicare Advantage business. Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes identified UnitedHealth and Humana as the insurers most vulnerable to the proposed changes, followed by CVS Health, Elevance Health, Centene and Molina Healthcare. Political pressure is creating another headwind. Senator Elizabeth Warren has called for breaking up vertically integrated healthcare conglomerates, specifically naming UnitedHealth, CVS and Cigna while supporting the proposed Break Up Big Medicine Act. Restrictions on insurers owning pharmacy benefit managers and healthcare providers could threaten UnitedHealth’s integrated Optum business model. Such measures could limit operational flexibility, increase compliance costs and potentially weaken the advantages of its vertically integrated structure. UnitedHealth shares have come under renewed selling pressure, falling approximately 9% on Wednesday after failing to consolidate gains above $400. The stock has retreated into the $320s, with investors reassessing the regulatory and operational risks facing the managed-care sector. Insurers are also facing elevated medical utilisation, particularly across outpatient and specialty services. If healthcare costs continue rising faster than premiums, underwriting profitability could deteriorate, adding pressure to earnings forecasts. UnitedHealth retains significant scale and cash-flow generation, but the combination of regulatory uncertainty, potential Medicare payment recoveries and higher medical costs leaves its shares vulnerable. Investors will be watching management guidance and the $350 area as an important technical reference, while a sustained recovery will likely require greater clarity on the potential financial impact of the CMS proposal.

title: Huskies Drop Game 1 vs. UNH - University of Connecticut Athletics
content: STORRS, Conn. — UConn men's hockey dropped game one of the two game series vs. New Hampshire by a final of 6-3 Thursday evening. The Huskies scored once in each period and finished with a 25-22 shot advantage, including a power-play goal in the second. UConn opened the first period a man down when Brendan Dunphy was called for a hooking penalty early in the first period. New Hampshire broke through five minutes in when a shot from the point beat Hendrickson. On the ensuing shift, Ethan Gardula found the back of the net following a Joey Muldowney steal, tying the game at one. Following the tie, both teams traded chances, but New Hampshire regained the lead when a save by Hendrickson bounced to a New Hampshire skater who fired it home for the 2-1 lead. The Huskies started the second period strong looking for the equalizer, but New Hampshire defense stayed strong. The Wildcats increased their lead early in the second when the Wildcats beat the Huskies defense creating an odd man rush. The Huskies answered on the power play shortly after when Alexandre Blais fired a one timer cutting the deficit to 3-2. The Huskies increased the pressure and were able to create another power play opportunity, but the Huskies were unable to find the back of the net with the man advantage. With the power play expiring, New Hampshire stole the puck at the blue line, and another odd man rush gave the Wildcats their fourth goal of the night once again giving the Wildcats the two-goal lead. The two teams battled in the third, but New Hampshire found the back of the net first increasing the lead to 5-2. Freshman Lirim Amidovski answered for UConn late in the period cutting the deficit to two. With under three minutes remaining in the game, UConn pulled Hendrickson in favor of an extra skater but with 53 seconds left in the game the Wildcats scored on the empty net securing the 6-3 win. The selling traces to a proposed rule from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), announced on November 16 by the Department of Health and Human Services, as reported by Medical Daily. According to the CMS proposed rule (CMS-6098-P), the agency plans to apply extrapolation to Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data validation (RADV) audits for payment year 2018 forward and to require insurers to remit improper payments found in those audits. The outlet tied the sell-off to the federal proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits and recover improper payments dating back to 2018, which it said could expose insurers to substantial financial liabilities. The move extended the 5.4% decline in UnitedHealth shares on November 17. The broader CRUSH proposal targets fraud, waste and abuse in Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP and the Marketplace, and HHS projects it would save nearly $90 billion in federal spending over 10 years, per Medical Daily.
